reply.text:
Grip giving out before your back does is common, and it's a training problem we can work on. A few things help:

- Dead hangs: a few sets of 20 to 40 seconds at the end of your session, adding time as they get easier.
- Heavy carries: farmer's carries or holding heavy dumbbells for time, a couple of times a week.
- Technique: squeeze the bar hard and pull the bar toward your chest, which keeps your forearms working in a stronger position than a loose, dangling grip.
- Chalk, if your gym allows it. It makes a real difference for most people.
- Straps on your heaviest pulling sets. That lets your back get the work when grip is the limit, as long as you train grip separately too.

If you'd like, I can add dead hangs or farmer's carries to your program.
